steps.text: Combine hot sauce, butter, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, cayenne, garlic powder, and salt in a pot over medium heat. Bring to a simmer while stirring with a whisk.

raw_recipe.headline: Buffalo Chicken Wing Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Chef John's recipe for the original Buffalo sauce is quick and easy to make with hot pepper sauce, butter, and vinegar for the best-tasting wings ever.

Discover the perfect balance of tangy, spicy, and buttery flavors that make Buffalo wings a beloved classic. Chef John guides you through each step, from creating the base sauce to adding the right amount of heat. Whether you're hosting a game day party or simply craving a flavorful snack, this homemade Buffalo Wing Sauce will have you licking your fingers and reaching for more. Don't miss out on this irresistible recipe that will become a staple in your kitchen.

review.reviewBody:
This the real thing! Very simple, very very good, and absolutely authentic taste *IF* you use Frank's Red Hot Sauce. Not Tabasco. Not nothin' else ... and you'll have the taste just like the originals from The Anchor Bar in Buffalo NY. And, just like Chef John says, butter is what you use ... not margarine. You should never buy store-bought wing sauce (waste of money, bad taste, and this stuff is soooo easy to make!). 
Suggestions:
- Omit the cayenne if you want your wings mild-to-medium-hot, 1/4 tsp as listed if you want it medium-hot, and, well, you get the idea. 
- Skip the extra salt (absolutely not necessary as all bottled hot sauce is incredibly salty anyway)
- Keep the sauce warm on the stove, and toss your hot-out-of-the-oven wings in a good amount of warmed hot-sauce, serve immediately
- Do not put these back in the oven to "dry" the sauce ... they're supposed to be saucy. 
- Keep some extra warmed hot sauce on the table for dipping (for those of us that need more hot-sauce punishment!)
- Lastly, serve with a real home-made blue cheese dressing, as there are several good ones on this site (choose one with less mayo-to-sour cream ratio) ... and don't forget the celery & carrot sticks to garnish for a crunch & cooling effect! 
Thanks for a great recipe, Chef John.

This is it!! I am from Buffalo and have lived away for many years. Every year when I visit I just can't get enough "wings", but now I can make them myself! Authentic recipe (sorry to those who don't like it, but this IS what wings taste like in Buffalo)... I deep fried the wings in peanut oil (355 degrees) in batches, then tossed all of the wings in the sauce - give em a good shake - with the lid on of course. Serve with blue cheese dressing, carrot and celery sticks. Tastes like home :) Thanks to Chef John!

The flavor of this recipe is so spot-on. Good ratios and a nice base level of heat with the provided amount of cayenne powder. Honestly, a 5-star recipe if it's just on flavor alone. I don't doubt it originated from Buffalo itself. However, if you want a smoother sauce that won't separate in the fridge, I recommend a change to the method. To start, melt the butter very slowly over very low heat on its own. Once the butter begins to melt, throw in a TB or two of hot water and steadily whisk that with the slowly melting butter until the butter is fully melted (should take a couple of minutes or so), then remove from heat. This will maintain the emulsion of the butter. Whisk in the hot sauce steadily (not all at once!), then the rest of the ingredients, and do not heat it up again. No need to cook this sauce. Compare my photo to the recipe photos of the sauce in the jar and you'll understand what broken sauce vs unbroken sauce means. Bonus points if you use clarified butter as it will be even smoother.

I think the basic recipe is great. I do dress it up slightly though. I use Texas Pete as my base. I add the garlic and some onion in an equal portion. I also add a 1/8 - 1/4 cup of veg. oil. Then I blend with emersion blender until it stays homogenized. (can also use wisk) This gives it much better mouth feel - it winds up "feeling" more sauce like and less thin. Also clings to wings better.

I agree this is basically the same as how I make mine, minus a few twists. After trying all types of hot sauces for the base Franks is the best hands down, although I do add a few splashes of Tabasco. For the people asking how to thicken this up make a slurry with arrowroot and the white vinegar and add sparingly for thickness. If you don't have arrowroot you can use corn starch, but its not quite as good and you cant over do the starch and therefore cant get it as thick. The differences in recipe I use are a few squirts of tabasco, a bif squeeze off a quarter lemon, dried basil, and I do not use the salt or garlic powder. Also for the absolute best chicken you can get, first smoke whole wings and let them chill in the fridge overnight or for 3 hours min. Then fry them before serving. This is hands down the best way to make the wings. Add this sauce and you'll have the best wings ever.
My go-to for medium buffalo flavor and heat profile. I add a couple of little squeezes of honey as a binder and for a touch of sweetness. Blend it till creamy and smooth with a blender. Perfection!
I coat the wings with corn starch then deep fry them. The coating on the wings after frying is perfect to hold onto the sauce. These wings are WAY much better than what you can get at a wing shop.
This recipe is really good. I made two changes - I added a little bit of honey and, more importantly, I blended the sauce to avoid separation and achieve an awesome texture. See attached pic.

I thought the sauce came out great! I only used one stick of butter 🧈 though and added some honey 🍯 and a lil cornstarch to thicken. The sauce stuck very nicely on the chicken. I used Louisiana hot sauce. It was spicy and sweet! Absolutely delicious 😋

Born, raised in Buffalo and in my youth was introduced to Wings. Folks, this is authentic. I'm a chicken wing snob, having endured so many train-wreck attempts to "perfect" what has already been perfected, and living in S. Florida I must say, I have had some gosh awful horrific "wings". This sauce tastes EXACTLY like the wings that I grew up with, and I mean exactly. Here's a tip though for as-close-as-you-can-possibly get to authentic, even though it's not the traditional cooking method: Air fry your wings at 370 degrees for 25 minutes, flip them and cook for 6 more minutes. Do this after placing them in a bag with a coupla tablespoons of olive oil. I'll swear by them. Every bit as good as LaNova's, Blasdell Pizza, or Anchor Bar. This sauce recipe though is the real deal.

I used butter, cayenne pepper sauce, garlic powder, cayenne pepper, salt, pepper. I didn’t have worcestershire sauce, I used malt vinegar instead of white (we’re moving and white vinegar is packed). I also added honey for a honey-hot Buffalo sauce. Delicious.

My son is allergic to eggs and for some reason I keep finding store bought sauces with egg added. So I’m used to making my own versions. I never tried buffalos sauce but this one came out great. My son loves it. I added to chicken Mac and cheese.

I’m one for using a recipe as a guideline while adding different ingredients to make it my own so that is what I did with this recipe. I added dried basil instead of the cayenne pepper and it is delicious.
Easy and delicious 🤤
I really like buffalo sauce thank you for this recipe. I am going to try to make it again. I think last time I used too much of everything.
The only problem with this recipe is it doesn't tell you how many wings the recipe will coat. If you're just cooking 12 wings, this is likely way too much
Excellent and authentic. I use Crystal Hot Sauce, but Franks is just as amazing. I finely dice garlic and mix in my sauce instead of the powder
I would add v garlic for my personal taste. Maybe sprinkle some parm on top.
This Buffalo Wing Sauce is so good! I used it for Buffalo Chicken Smashed Tacos and it was so good! Will totally be making this again!
this taste great and I doubled it.
